preamble: Lambdacism is the shift of a sound (often [r]) to [l]. It is a common liquid interchange, frequently occurring as a form of dissimilation or in specific dialectal developments.

examples.note: Historical shift of [r] to [l] in Eastern Indo-Aryan Prakrits.
Everyday Bangkok speech regularly replaces /r/ with [l]; careful speech keeps the tap or trill

sources: Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages.
Smyth, D. (2002). Thai: An Essential Grammar. Routledge.
